newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The time has come to increase the size of the police service and government is committeed to lifting the moratorium on police recruiting, Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said.

- Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd lifted headline earnings 42.3 percent to 595 million rand for the six months to September, attributing the better-than-expected results to cost containment and wider margins.

- Gencor has a five-year plan to build up an offshore gold division with a reserve base equal in size to Gengold, the group's local gold division, which could be listed on an international stock exchange.

- Government and the oil industry are considering a fresh bid to promote the use of unleaded gasoline amid signs that its share of the 10.2 million litres a year petrol market has stagnated well below the target level of about 20 percent.
- Samgro, the banking and financial services holding company controlled by retail tycoon Christo Wiese, is tipped to take a sizeable stake in NBS Holdings in a multi-billion rand deal.
- Absa said net profit in the six months to September 30 increased 42.3 percent, a better-than-expected rise that chief executive Danie Cronje said would be tough to repeat in the second half.

- Virgin Atlatic Airways will consider introducing direct flights from Johannesburg to New York in conjunction with a South African airline next year, the company's general manager in southern Africa said.
- Gold markets were looking shaky late on Monday as the metal fixed at $375.10 an ounce in London in the morning, its lowest level for 20 months.
- South African gold production will slump further to 492-495 tones this year, the lowest level in 40 years, according to Chamber of Mines' economist Roger Baxter.

- Archbishiop Desmond Tutu on Monday sharply rebuked members of his Truth and Reconciliation Commission, ordering them to stop saying things during public hearins which could undermine the commission's effort to appear even-handed.
- After surviving two hijackings and an armed robbery, all within a month, Lester Milton and his wife Joy are ready to leave their home in Lombardy East in Johannesburg.
